clue.text: Naval ship requiring quarantine?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a warship that launches aircraft
second meaning: someone who spreads an infection and must be isolated

explanation.surface: A warship held offshore because a disease has broken out among the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second definition describes the person rather than naming them.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an aircraft-launching warship and a person who harbours and passes on a disease, someone who must be isolated.

clue.text: Spotted horse thatês white, not black

parts.note: surface reading: a horse with patches that might be a piebald
setter's reading: the patched horse whose second colour is anything but black, usually brown

explanation.surface: Someone describing a patchy horse at a show and correcting the colours.
explanation.walkthrough: A piebald is black and white; this term covers a horse with white and some other colour, so the 'not black' is the distinction being tested.
explanation.definitionFit: Equestrian vocabulary distinguishes coats with white patches on brown or chestnut from the black-and-white piebald coat.

clue.text: They tend to rush over certain points

indicators.note: turned over, as in flipped, so the word for rush runs from back to front

parts.note: to run is to rush
south, east, south: compass points

explanation.surface: Some people have a habit of hurrying past particular details.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They tend to' reads as 'they are inclined to', but 'tend' is the verb of caring. Compass points are a stock source of single letters N, E, S, W.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospital staff who look after patients are the people who tend the sick, so the plural fits the pronoun phrase.

clue.text: Whip up strike in sporting association

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the implement swung up and brought down to hit a ball
second meaning: a society that runs a course for members

explanation.surface: Agitators stirring up industrial action inside a sports body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Whip up strike' sounds like rousing workers to down tools; it actually describes the swing of an iron or driver.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the stick used on the links to hit the ball and the members' organisation that owns a course.

clue.text: Loan shark certain to be found in the City

indicators.note: something found in a place sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, the crossword's favourite city
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A crooked moneylender is bound to turn up in London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' looks like London's Square Mile, home of finance; here it is the ancient Sumerian city of Ur.
explanation.definitionFit: A lender charging extortionate interest is the old term for what is now called a loan shark.

clue.text: The bloom of life?

parts.note: surface reading: the prime or flowering of existence
setter's reading: the stage when a young body blossoms into adulthood

explanation.surface: A poetic phrase for the best years of one's life.
explanation.definitionFit: Adolescence brings sexual maturity, the developmental stage when a child's body flowers into an adult one.

clue.text: Industrial action court

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a strike in which workers leave
second meaning: to go out with someone romantically, as in the old phrase

explanation.surface: A labour dispute being heard at a tribunal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a law court; it is the verb meaning to date, as in 'walking out' with a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a noun for workers downing tools and leaving, and an old-fashioned verb phrase for dating someone.

clue.text: Reckless person pulled up short

parts.note: surface reading: a rash rider or driver brought to a sudden halt
setter's reading: Shakespeare's rash Harry Percy, whose life was cut off at Shrewsbury

explanation.surface: A daredevil forced to stop abruptly.
explanation.walkthrough: Harry Percy, nicknamed for his impetuosity, is killed by Prince Hal in Henry IV Part 1, his career stopped early.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of the impetuous Percy became a common noun for any rash, hot-headed individual.

clue.text: Put a simpler form of material for test

indicators.note: a new form of some words means their letters are reshaped into another arrangement

parts.note: the three words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: An instruction to draft an easier version of an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material for test' suggests exam content; it means chemical paper used to test acidity.
explanation.definitionFit: Paper treated with dye that changes colour shows whether a solution is acid or alkali, a laboratory testing material.

clue.text: There aren't many of these coins left in Europe

definitions.text: There aren't many of these coins left in Europe

parts.words: There aren't many of these coins left in Europe
parts.note: surface reading: an old currency that has mostly gone out of circulation
setter's reading: also the headgear of reigning monarchs, of which Europe keeps only a few

explanation.surface: A collector remarking that a certain old coinage has become scarce on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British five-shilling pieces bore this name; the same word is the regal headpieces of the few monarchies left.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a historic coin denomination and the jewelled symbols of royalty, both now rare.

clue.text: Told, but possibly not needing to be

definitions.meaning: second meaning: already knowledgeable, so perhaps not requiring to be told

explanation.surface: Someone was given information they may well have known already.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a riddle: a well-read person may not need telling.
explanation.definitionFit: The participle means notified, and as an adjective describes someone knowledgeable who already has the facts.

clue.text: Julietês town is just not on for her

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for a woman's name

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken out of the place name

parts.note: Romeo and Juliet is set in this Italian city
taken as written

explanation.surface: Juliet's home town disapproves of a woman's conduct: it's just not on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just not on' reads as an idiom of disapproval; really it says drop ON from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords often define a female forename by a pronoun; this is a woman's given name, as in the singer Lynn.

clue.text: It looks like the military is involved

definitions.note: a phrase describing the quality rather than a noun

indicators.note: involved means tangled or complicated, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: the two words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: A suspicion that the army has a hand in something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looks like' seems to mean 'apparently'; read literally, a thing that looks like another has a resemblance to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Resemblance between two things is when one looks like the other, which is what this abstract noun names.

clue.text: Is an orator lost and speechless without it?

definitions.text: Is an orator lost and speechless without it?

parts.words: Is an orator lost and speechless without it?
parts.note: surface reading: a speaker who dries up without notes
setter's reading: someone who cannot find where people live is lost without the directory of contacts

explanation.surface: A speechmaker who would be stuck dumb without a prompt.
explanation.walkthrough: An address is a formal speech, so an orator's book sounds like a speech script; really it is the list of where friends live.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal directory listing where contacts live; without one you are lost for where to send letters.

clue.text: Agree end will be terrible for traitor

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad state, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the two words used letter for letter

explanation.surface: Settling the end of a deal will go badly for a turncoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter who abandons their cause or side for the enemy is a turncoat, the same as one who betrays.

clue.text: Elderly crew of experienced campaigners

parts.note: elderly means aged
hands are crew members on a ship

explanation.surface: An ageing team of veteran political campaigners.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes veterans with long practice at something, people who have seen many battles before.

clue.text: A relative right in the midst of trouble

indicators.note: in the midst of puts one thing in the middle of another

parts.note: bother means trouble
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A family member caught up in some difficulty.
explanation.definitionFit: A male sibling is a kinsman, a member of one's family, so any such person counts as a relation.

clue.text: Reported to be held at gunpoint

definitions.meaning: first meaning: written up by a journalist
second meaning: kept in the sights of a weapon

explanation.surface: News that someone is said to have been taken hostage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reported to be' looks like hearsay framing; it is a separate meaning, as a journalist reports on a story.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalists say a story was dealt with in the news, and a gunman keeps a target within aim; one word does both.

clue.text: Can-opener?

parts.note: surface reading: a kitchen tool for tins
setter's reading: can is slang for a jail, and its opener is the entrance swung open

explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is American slang for jail, so its opener is the way in or out of the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for jail is can, so the barrier that opens to let inmates in or out is the jail's opener.

clue.text: Cry out — to the police?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: give a shrill cry
second meaning: inform on someone, slang for grassing

explanation.surface: A cry for help addressed to the police.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes it one appeal; the second sense is underworld slang for informing on accomplices.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to make a high-pitched cry, and in criminal slang to betray associates by informing.

clue.text: Aim by listener to win affection

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
the ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A goal set by an audience member hoping to be liked.
explanation.definitionFit: To make oneself loved or liked by someone is to gain their fondness, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Fall for a medical man at work

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Falling in love with a doctor while he is on duty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fall for' looks like a phrasal verb about attraction; 'Fall' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun or verb the word means a descent, a plunge or tumble, the same as a fall.

clue.text: Try hard to get free labour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to wriggle and fight against restraint
second meaning: to toil with great effort

explanation.surface: An effort to obtain workers without paying them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free labour' reads as unpaid workers, but the split falls between 'free' and 'labour'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both fighting to escape a hold and toiling with difficulty at a task.

clue.text: Recompensed for returning a nappy

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: repaid means recompensed

explanation.surface: Getting paid back for bringing back a nappy to the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the American word for what Britons call a nappy, a baby's cloth or disposable pad.
explanation.definitionFit: American English uses this word for the absorbent garment worn by babies that the British call a nappy.

clue.text: Looks at with an expression of friendliness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: gazes at or considers
second meaning: good wishes sent at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone gazes at another with a warm, friendly look.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means observes or considers; the plural noun is the kind wishes sent, as in 'give him my best'.

clue.text: They have evil ends in films

definitions.text: They have evil ends in films

parts.words: They have evil ends in films
parts.note: surface reading: characters with wicked aims on screen
setter's reading: villains who meet a nasty death in the final reel

explanation.surface: Movie characters pursuing wicked purposes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Evil ends' means both wicked goals and unpleasant deaths; screen villains have both.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal word for the villains of a film or story, the wicked characters opposed to the heroes.
